name: Tokyo LiF bolometer
full_name: Tokyo LiF bolometer dark matter search
summary: A historical WIMP search by the University of Tokyo team using cryogenic lithium-fluoride calorimeters at Kamioka, probing spin-dependent interactions with light nuclei.
detection_principle: WIMP scattering on Li/F nuclei produces a tiny temperature rise. Cryogenic calorimetry avoids limitations associated with relying solely on scintillation energy measurements and quenching.

sites.name: Kamioka Observatory
sites.location: Kamioka underground experimental facility, Hida, Gifu Prefecture
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The first underground-search paper identifies a 2001–2002 running window; the status refers to that published run.

collaboration.name: Tokyo LiF bolometer Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

key_parameters.name: Array
key_parameters.value: Eight LiF calorimeters, with a total mass of 168 g

results.summary: LiF nuclear-recoil data constrain spin-dependent WIMPs.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
